title: Jump Game VII
description: Determine reachability in a binary string with a bounded jump range, using DP accelerated by an incrementally maintained sliding window count.

blocks.text: Given a binary string s of length n, and integers minJump and maxJump, you start at index 0. From index i, you may move to index j if i + minJump <= j <= min(i + maxJump, n - 1) and s[j] == '0'. Return true if it is possible to reach index n - 1.

blocks.caption: A sliding window tracks how many reachable positions fall within the valid jump range for each index.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Field","Details"],"rows":[["Input","s (binary string), minJump, maxJump"],["Start","Index 0 (guaranteed s[0] == '0')"],["Move rule","From i, land on any j with i+minJump <= j <= min(i+maxJump, n-1) where s[j] == '0'"],["Goal","Determine if index n - 1 is reachable"]]}

blocks.text: Reachability with a bounded jump range is a DP problem where dp[i] depends on whether ANY position in a sliding window [i - maxJump, i - minJump] is itself reachable. Whenever a DP transition needs "does any true value exist in a sliding window," a running window count (incrementing as positions enter, decrementing as they leave) answers it in O(1) per step, avoiding a full rescan.

blocks.title: Connection
blocks.text: Similar in spirit to Maximum Number of Robots Within Budget: both maintain a running aggregate over a sliding window instead of recomputing it from scratch at each step.

Picture a frog on a row of lily pads, some marked unsafe ('1') and some safe ('0'). The frog can only land on safe pads, and each hop must travel between minJump and maxJump pads forward. The question is whether the frog can reach the final pad.

blocks.caption: A moving window tracks which recently-reachable pads are still within jumping range.

items: dp[i] is true only if s[i] == '0' AND some dp[j] is true for j in the window [i - maxJump, i - minJump].
As i increases by one, the window also shifts by one: a new index enters at i - minJump, and an old index leaves at i - maxJump - 1.
Tracking a running count of true dp values currently in the window avoids rescanning the whole window at every step.

blocks.title: Answer
blocks.text: dp[5] is true, so index 5 (the last index) is reachable via 0 -> 3 -> 5, matching the expected output of true.

The direct DP checks, for each index i, every position in its window [i-maxJump, i-minJump] to see if any is reachable, stopping early on the first true. This is correct but can rescan overlapping windows across consecutive indices.

Since the window for index i and index i+1 overlap heavily (shifted by exactly one position), maintain a running windowCount: add dp[i - minJump] to the count when it enters the window (at the new right edge), and subtract dp[i - maxJump - 1] when it leaves (falls off the old left edge). dp[i] is then simply s[i] == '0' and windowCount > 0.
For each index, scan its entire jump window directly to check if any position in it is reachable.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Metric","Value","Why"],"rows":[["Time","O(n * (maxJump - minJump))","Each index scans up to maxJump - minJump + 1 window positions"],["Space","O(n)","The dp array"]]}

blocks.title: Bottleneck
blocks.text: When maxJump - minJump is large, rescanning heavily overlapping windows at every index wastes work that a running count avoids entirely.

Maintain windowCount as a running total of true dp values within the current window. At each step, add the newly entered position's dp value and subtract the one that just left, then set dp[i] based on whether s[i] is '0' and windowCount is positive. This makes each step O(1), for O(n) total.

items: A quick check first: if s[n-1] is not '0', the answer is immediately false.
At each i, add dp[i - minJump] if it exists and is true (entering the window).
Subtract dp[i - maxJump - 1] if it exists and is true (leaving the window), then set dp[i] from windowCount.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Approach","Time","Space"],"rows":[["Brute Force, rescan window each index","O(n * (maxJump - minJump))","O(n)"],["Optimized, running window count","O(n)","O(n)"]]}

items: A DP transition needing "does any true value exist in a sliding window" is answered in O(1) per step with a running add/remove count.
The window for consecutive indices shifts by exactly one position, which is exactly what makes incremental maintenance possible instead of a full rescan.
This add-on-entry, subtract-on-exit pattern reapplies to any sliding-window aggregate, whether a count, sum, or max (via a monotonic deque).

blocks.text: Jump Game VII is solved with dp[i] = true when s[i] is '0' and some reachable position exists in the sliding window [i-maxJump, i-minJump]. Maintaining that window's reachable count incrementally, adding entries and removing exits as the window shifts by one each step, turns an O(n * jumpRange) brute force into an O(n) sweep.
